source2: Pierre Leriche, 'Bactria i. Pre-Islamic period', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/bactria/bactria-i-pre-islamic-period/
notes: Nomads (Yuezhi/Tochari, Asii, Saraucae) overran Bactria; c.130-128 BCE Zhang Qian found it in petty principalities under Yuezhi domination. Earlier Eucratid-Euthydemid conflict; Ai Khanoum abandoned c.147. Database end 125 BCE slightly late.

source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'China: Foreign affairs under Yangdi' (Sui collapse and Tang founding), Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/China/Foreign-affairs-under-Yangdi
notes: Empire-wide revolts after failed Korean wars (from 613). Sui official Li Yuan rebelled 617, took Chang'an, enthroned puppet Gongdi, proclaimed Tang 618 after Yangdi's murder. Tang kept Sui institutions, so T0 arguable.

successor: Alawi dynasty (took Marrakesh 1668-69; Shabana tribal chief held it 1659-68)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'North Africa: Morocco under sharifian dynasties', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/North-Africa/Political-fragmentation-and-the-triumph-of-Islamic-culture-c-1250-c-1500
notes: Post-1603 succession war divided Morocco into principalities (Dila'iyya etc.); last Saadi killed 1659 by maternal Shabana kin (lead only). Internal Alawis from Tafilalt took Marrakesh 1669. Home area 'Niger Inland Delta' is wrong.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Western Africa: The Islamic revolution in the western Sudan', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/western-Africa/The-Islamic-revolution-in-the-western-Sudan
notes: Torodbe clerics overthrew the Muslim but 'exploitative' Denyanke satigis, founding a theocratic almamate after 1776 (Sulayman Bal, Abdul Qadir). 18th-century succession wars and Moorish/Moroccan interference per leads, not in cited pages.

successor: Northern Song (Zhao Kuangyin took over the Later Zhou court at Kaifeng)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Taizu (emperor of Song dynasty)', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Taizu-emperor-of-Song-dynasty
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'China: The Song dynasty', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/China/The-Song-dynasty
notes: Later Zhou palace-army commander Zhao Kuangyin, acclaimed by troops in 960, pledged to spare the imperial family and councillors; Song kept Kaifeng and court. Coup-style dynastic change within same apparatus. Database end 970 wrong; 960.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Qutaybah ibn Muslim', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Qutaybah-ibn-Muslim
source2: Etienne de La Vaissiere, 'Sogdiana iii. History and archeology', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/sogdiana-iii-history-and-archeology/
notes: Qutayba b. Muslim's Arab armies conquered Sogdiana from 705: Bukhara 706-709, Samarkand 712; local rulers remained as tributaries. Sogdiana was a loose set of principalities; no specific pre-conquest crisis found in sources opened.

successor: Habr Yunis Sultanate continued under nominal British protectorate (British Somaliland)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Somalia: The imperial partition', Encyclopaedia Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/Somalia/The-great-Somali-migrations
source2: None: no second citable source could be opened (web search and fetch budgets exhausted)
notes: 1884-86 British protection treaties left the interior undisturbed and territory not ceded; Habr Yunis sultanate persisted (Dervish war from 1899) until interior administration c.1920 (leads). 1870s-80s Awad-Nur succession war (leads). Start 1300 too early (c.1769).

Daylamite Buyids, based in Fars/Khuzestan, entered Baghdad 19 Dec 945 without a fight after the amir al-umara regime broke down; caliphs kept prestige, no political power. Prior anarchy and Turkic-guard domination. Database 946 vs 945.

successor: Middle Elamite Kingdom (Shutrukid Elam), then Second Dynasty of Isin
notes: Elamite kings Shutruk-Nahhunte and Kutir-Nahhunte invaded Babylonia, destroying the Kassite dynasty c.1155 BCE; Kassite power was 'already weakened by local insurrection'. Isin II rose afterwards. Database 1150 close (chronology-dependent).
